transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
Police in the United Kingdom say several people have been arrested overnight
in connection to explosive devices found near Fairford,
a U.K. military base in southwest England that's used by the U.S. service members for strikes on Iran.
Assistant Chief Constable Richard Ocone says police evacuated dozens of homes near the base.
As a precaution, around 85 households have been advised to evacuate while these examinations take place.
And a bomb squad is on the scene as armed officers reportedly guard the entrance.
This base has been the scene of protests over the British government's decision this summer
to allow the U.S. to use it for staging limited strikes on Iranian missile sites.
But Iran says bombers flying from the base have been used for strikes beyond the original usage mandate.
Tehran says that made the base a legitimate target in the ongoing U.S. war against Iran.
The White House had told Congress it plans to cancel $810 million dollars in health care and educational-related programs.
As in Peers-Maralison reports, one prominent Republican isn't happy about that.
In a statement on X, Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins said the move, known as a pocket rescission, is unlawful.
Collins, an incumbent Republican from Maine running for reelection, also said that the rescissions were intended to "undermine Congress's constitutional power of the purse."
Regardless of how this separation of powers dispute is resolved, there are other cuts to social safety net programs that were in the one big beautiful bill that are just now kicking in.
And they're hurting people who depend on Medicaid and food assistance.
That's another reason, along with higher prices at the pump or 7 percent mortgages, that voters say they are angry and economically stressed.
A bad sign for the incumbent party just weeks away from the election.
Maralison, NPR News.
A massive nor'easter is pounding parts of the Northeast with coastal flooding and strong winds for a second straight day.
Steve Kastenbaum reports some coastal towns are seeing their worst flooding in more than a decade.
High tides continue to bring more flooding, especially in towns along the Jersey Shore.
In Atlantic City, floodwaters hit their highest level since Superstorm Sandy in 2012.
Wind gusts reached 60 miles per hour in some areas.
A public housing employee in New York died when he was hit by a falling tree branch.
Governor Kathy Hochul said dangerous winds will stick around for a while.
It's ferocious and it needs to be taken seriously.
Tens of thousands of power outages were reported from Maine down to North Carolina.
Beach erosion is significant in some areas.
High tides were made worse thanks to Saturday's full moon.
The nor'easter is expected to sit around off the coast of New Jersey and Long Island through Monday.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Kastenbaum in New York.
This is NPR News.
Israel has closed several of its military checkpoints in the occupied West Bank,
and that move caused traffic jams for Palestinians.
As NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports, this comes ahead of Israel's national elections.
Ali Hussein Yusuf Abdullah was trying to cross one checkpoint near Ramallah on foot
in hopes of visiting his sick aunt.
He said he'd been waiting more than two hours when he talked with NPR's producer in the West Bank,
Nuha Musleh, who said dozens of cars were backed up at the crossing for hours.
The further limiting of movement comes after a Palestinian car ramming attack seriously wounded an Israeli soldier,
the son of Israel's ambassador to the U.S.
Days earlier, a Palestinian gunman killed an Israeli settler,
while there has been a wave of settler violence against Palestinians.
Meanwhile, Israel has ramped up its military presence in the occupied territory,
fearing an explosion of violence as Election Day draws closer.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
Two giant pandas are on their way to the Atlanta Zoo,
leaving Chengdu in southwestern China earlier today.
In Washington last week, Chinese President Xi Jinping said the pandas would arrive in the U.S. in the coming days,
and their arrival, their on loan from China, is one of the few concrete outcomes of the state visit.
Atlanta Zoo has been without pandas since 2024, when the last ones went back home.
Jinping, a male, and Fuxuang, a female, both adults, will stay for 10 years.
They're both six years old.
The pandalone program is part of China's global diplomacy program as an expression of goodwill.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News.
That's plus.npr.org.

topics.text: Several people arrested in U.K. in connection with explosive devices found near Fairford military base
White House plans to cancel $810 million in health care and educational programs; Senator Collins calls move unlawful
Massive nor'easter pounds Northeast for second day with coastal flooding and strong winds affecting multiple states
Israel closes military checkpoints in occupied West Bank, causing traffic jams for Palestinians ahead of elections
Two giant pandas from China arrive at Atlanta Zoo on ten-year loan as diplomatic gesture
